title: A bill to require the Securities and Exchange Commission to issue rules relating to the use of artificial intelligence by public companies, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The bill proposes that the Securities and Exchange Commission create rules governing how public companies use artificial intelligence in their operations. It also includes additional provisions for oversight, reporting, and other related corporate responsibilities.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to make sure AI systems are safe, trustworthy, and reliable before they are put into use. It sets standards for research, requires thorough testing, and demands transparency so people can confidently rely on AI technology.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the CISA Director, to establish a pilot program that employs AI for defending critical infrastructure from cyber threats. The program aims to test and develop AI-driven tools to strengthen cybersecurity for essential services and infrastructure.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a dedicated group within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to focus on the safety and resilience of AI systems. The law directs this task force to develop standards, conduct risk assessments, and coordinate with other agencies and industry to protect critical infrastructure from AI‑related threats.

title: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency a pilot program to be known as the "BRIDGE AI Mission Program" to recruit and manage artificial intelligence and emerging technology professionals on a temporary basis to support the core mission of the Agency, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This amendment creates a new pilot program inside the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency called the BRIDGE AI Mission Program. The program will temporarily recruit and manage AI and emerging technology professionals to help the Agency carry out its core missions and other related tasks.

title: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to lead cybersecurity efforts relating to the secure adoption, discovery, identification, authorization, monitoring, accountability, and risk management of artificial intelligence agents operating on executive agency information systems, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Homeland Security, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The amendment updates the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to make the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Director responsible for overseeing cybersecurity related to artificial intelligence agents used on executive agency information systems. This includes ensuring secure adoption, discovery, identification, authorization, monitoring, accountability, and risk management of such AI agents, while also addressing other related cybersecurity measures.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to regulate how AI systems are built and used, focusing on safety, transparency, and accountability. It sets out guidelines that require developers to conduct risk assessments, provide clear explanations of how AI works, and establish oversight mechanisms to protect users and society from potential harms.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 is a U.S. law designed to stop artificial intelligence systems from secretly working together to fix prices or reduce competition. It requires companies to monitor algorithmic behavior, report any signs of collusion, and imposes penalties for those that facilitate such unlawful coordination.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 aims to help small businesses adopt and use AI by providing training resources, funding, and support. It establishes educational programs and initiatives so small businesses can develop and responsibly deploy AI technologies.

title: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency the National Cyber and AI Investigations Board to investigate significant cyber incidents, cyber incidents involving terrorism, and cyber incidents involving artificial intelligence, to determine root causes and develop recommendations to prevent similar incidents and address terrorism threats to the United States, including threats relating to the malicious use of information systems or artificial intelligence by covered foreign adversaries, including terrorist organizations, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The bill proposes to update the Homeland Security Act of 2002 by creating a new board inside the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. This National Cyber and AI Investigations Board would examine major cyber incidents—including those involving terrorism or AI—determine their root causes, and recommend ways to prevent future threats, especially from foreign adversaries and terrorist groups.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on the construction of new AI data centers, allowing time to assess their broader impacts. It gives lawmakers an opportunity to develop guidelines and regulations before new facilities are built or expanded.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to address the ecological footprint of AI technologies, setting standards for energy use, carbon emissions, and resource consumption. It requires developers and users to monitor, report, and reduce environmental impacts, encouraging greener AI practices and compliance with national sustainability goals.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on building new data centers that primarily support AI services. It aims to curb environmental impact, manage energy use, and address concerns over rapid AI infrastructure expansion.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to tackle the ecological effects of AI technology. It seeks to set regulations on AI development and deployment to reduce carbon footprints, manage resource consumption, and promote sustainable practices.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act establishes guidelines and requirements for the development, deployment, and oversight of AI systems to protect national security and public safety. It imposes regulatory oversight on AI developers and users, requiring risk assessments, safety standards, and transparency measures.

title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 establishes a framework for regulating artificial intelligence across different industries, setting sector‑specific standards and compliance requirements. It creates oversight mechanisms to manage risks, protect consumers, and promote responsible AI development and deployment.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is intended to curb the practice of charging excessively high prices for AI products and services. The law also targets the prevention of wage fixing among AI industry workers, promoting fair compensation.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are at risk of going bankrupt because of problems in the AI market. Instead, Congress should focus on helping all Americans who have been harmed.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a law designed to regulate the use of artificial intelligence, setting rules to protect privacy, safety, and fairness for people. It requires companies to assess risks, be transparent about AI systems, and follow clear guidelines so that AI benefits society while reducing potential harm.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 aims to keep medical diagnosis and treatment in the hands of licensed human doctors, banning AI systems from making or providing medical decisions. It is designed to protect patients by ensuring that all medical care remains subject to professional oversight and accountability.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 aims to hold companies responsible for how their automated decision systems affect consumers and society. It requires businesses to assess and disclose algorithmic risks, particularly bias and discrimination, and to implement corrective measures to protect public interest.
